content.text:
Build real user management and role-based access control for this app,
replacing the currently-hardcoded dev auth. Three roles: Master, Admin,
Staff (no Contractor role - out of scope for this pass).

## Role capabilities (final design - implement exactly this, don't
## reinterpret)

- Master: creates any account (Admin or Staff). Full CRUD on Schedules,
  Inspections, Defects, Rectifications, plus Endorse.
- Admin: creates Staff accounts only (cannot create another Admin or a
  Master). Full CRUD on Schedules (including creating and assigning them to
  Staff), full CRUD + full visibility on Inspections/Defects/Rectifications
  across every staff member, plus Endorse.
- Staff: cannot manage any accounts.
  - Schedules: read-only, and ONLY schedules assigned to them - EXCEPT they
    CAN update just the `status` field (Scheduled/Assigned/In
    Progress/Completed/Cancelled) on their own assigned schedules. They
    cannot create, delete, or edit any other field (date, lift company,
    town council, reassignment) on a schedule.
  - Inspections: can create/edit, but only for a schedule assigned to them
    (or with no schedule link at all, if that's already allowed).
  - Defects: can log freely, not restricted to lifts/schedules assigned to
    them.
  - Rectifications: can create/submit. Cannot call the endorse endpoint
    under any circumstance - that's Admin/Master only.

There is no "Manager" role - retire that label entirely. Every place in the
current codebase that checks `role === 'Admin' || role === 'Manager'`
should become a proper 3-role check per the table above, not a straight
find-and-replace of "Manager" with "Admin".

## Backend

1. New User model (backend/src/models/users/User.js): name, email (unique),
   passwordHash, role (enum: Master/Admin/Staff), createdBy (ref User, so
   it's auditable who created each account), isDeleted (soft delete,
   consistent with every other model in this app - see
   backend/src/utils/cascadeDelete.js for the pattern), timestamps.

2. Auth: bcrypt for password hashing, JWT for sessions. Endpoints:
   POST /api/auth/login (email+password -> JWT with role/userId claims),
   and account management endpoints (create/list/deactivate users) gated by
   the account-creation rules above (Master creates anyone, Admin creates
   Staff only, enforced server-side, not just hidden in the UI).

3. Middleware: requireAuth + requireRole(...roles), wired into the routes
   that already have a standing TODO for this:
   - backend/src/routes/lifts/liftRoutes.js
   - backend/src/routes/defects/defectsRoutes.js
   - backend/src/routes/inspections/inspectionsRoutes.js
   - backend/src/routes/rectifications/rectificationsRoutes.js (this one's
     TODO specifically calls out restricting the endorse route further -
     do that: PATCH /:id/endorse requires Admin or Master specifically, not
     just "can edit")
   - backend/src/routes/scheduling/ currently has NO such TODO/comment at
     all - add the same auth gating here too, it was apparently missed
     when the other route files got their TODOs.

4. Schedule model (backend/src/models/scheduling/Schedule.js): add
   `assignedStaffId` (ObjectId ref User, nullable) as the real relational
   link - the existing `assignedInspector` free-text field can stay as a
   display snapshot (same pattern as liftCode/block snapshots elsewhere in
   this codebase) but must no longer be the source of truth for access
   control. Write a migration/backfill step (follow the pattern in
   backend/src/utils/cascadeDelete.js's cleanupOrphans, or add to seed.js)
   that maps existing `assignedInspector` name strings to real User
   accounts where possible, and leaves `assignedStaffId: null` where it
   can't confidently match - don't silently guess wrong.

5. Query scoping: listSchedules (schedulingController.js) must filter to
   `assignedStaffId: req.user._id` when the caller's role is Staff (Admin/
   Master see everything, unfiltered by this). updateSchedule must reject
   any Staff-submitted field other than `status`, and reject entirely if
   the schedule isn't assigned to that Staff user. createInspection
   (inspectionController.js) must additionally verify, for a Staff caller,
   that the referenced scheduleId's assignedStaffId matches their own user
   id - this extends the existing assertScheduleMatchesLift check, doesn't
   replace it.

## Frontend

1. Replace frontend/src/context/AuthContext.jsx's hardcoded dev user with
   a real login flow: a login page, JWT stored (e.g. localStorage) and
   attached as an Authorization header on every API call, and a logout
   action.

2. Update every `canEdit = user.role === 'Admin' || user.role ===
   'Manager'` check (Lifts.jsx, InspectionsStep.jsx, DefectsStep.jsx,
   RectificationsStep.jsx, SchedulingStep.jsx) to reflect the real 3-role
   matrix above instead of a flat binary - e.g. SchedulingStep.jsx's "Add
   Schedule" button and full-field edit should be Admin/Master only, but
   Staff still needs a way to update just the status of their own assigned
   schedules (don't just hide everything behind the same old canEdit flag).

3. EndorseButton.jsx should only render for Admin/Master, per its own
   existing TODO comment.

4. New account management screen: Master sees and can create
   Admin+Staff, Admin sees and can create Staff only - enforce this in the
   UI but rely on the backend enforcement above as the real guard, not this
   screen.

5. SchedulingStep.jsx / the Lift Workflow's schedule list should filter to
   "assigned to me" automatically for a Staff-role user (the backend already
   scopes the query, but make sure the UI doesn't imply they could see more).

## Out of scope for this pass
No Contractor/lift-company-facing role or portal - that's a separate,
larger piece of work, not part of this prompt.

## Testing
Add tests covering: a Staff user cannot create/delete a schedule (403), can
update only status on their own assigned schedule, cannot touch a schedule
assigned to someone else, cannot call the endorse endpoint, and an Admin
cannot create another Admin account (only Master can).


**There is no `middleware/` directory at all** — no auth middleware exists yet. There is also **no `User` model** anywhere in the repo (only `useRectifications.js` on the frontend matched a "User" glob, which is unrelated).

Important quirk: `backend/src/models/lifts/Lift.js` has **no `isDeleted` field** — it's the odd one out (hard-delete presumably in `liftController.js`), while Defect, Inspection, Rectification, and Schedule all have `isDeleted: { type: Boolean, default: false }`.

## 2. `backend/src/utils/cascadeDelete.js` (full file, 119 lines)

Pattern: soft-delete only, chain is `Schedule -> Inspection -> Defect -> Rectification`.
- `cascadeFromDefects(defectIds)`: `Rectification.updateMany({ defectId: {$in}, isDeleted:false }, {isDeleted:true})`.
- `cascadeFromInspections(inspectionIds)`: soft-deletes Defects by `inspectionId`, then recurses into `cascadeFromDefects`.
- `cascadeFromSchedule(scheduleId)`: soft-deletes Inspections by `scheduleId`, then recurses into `cascadeFromInspections`.
- `cleanupOrphans()`: a repair pass, safe to re-run anytime — (1) backfills `isDeleted:false` on any legacy docs missing the field (important: `{isDeleted:false}` filters don't match docs where the field is absent), then (2) walks parent links to soft-delete any child left dangling by e.g. a direct DB edit. Requires `Schedule` lazily via `require()` inside the function to avoid a circular import.

This is the exact pattern to replicate for a `User` model if you want cascade/orphan handling for user-authored records (e.g. `createdBy`/`assignedTo` references), and `cleanupOrphans` is the natural place to add a backfill step for a new field (e.g., migrating existing free-text `assignedInspector` strings to a `assignedInspectorUserId` ref).

## 3. `backend/src/models/scheduling/Schedule.js` (full file, 41 lines)

```js
const STATUS_VALUES = ['Scheduled', 'Assigned', 'In Progress', 'Completed', 'Cancelled'];
const scheduleSchema = new mongoose.Schema({
  townCouncil: { type: String, required: true, trim: true },
  liftCompany: { type: String, required: true, trim: true },
  blockAddress: { type: String, required: true, trim: true },
  liftId: { type: mongoose.Schema.Types.ObjectId, ref: 'Lift', default: null },
  scheduledDate: { type: Date, required: true },
  assignedInspector: { type: String, trim: true, default: '' },   // <-- free-text string, NOT a ref
  status: { type: String, enum: STATUS_VALUES, default: 'Scheduled' },
  notes: { type: String, trim: true, default: '' },
  isDeleted: { type: Boolean, default: false },
}, { timestamps: true });
```
`assignedInspector` is currently a **plain trimmed string** (e.g. `'Jessica S.'` in seed.js), not an ObjectId ref to any User model. If you want inspector assignment to reference real Users, this field needs to change type (or you add a new `assignedInspectorId` ref field alongside it for backward compat with existing string data — mirrors the `liftId` "optional forward link" pattern already used here).

## 4. Route files — exact content & TODOs

- **`liftRoutes.js`**: `TODO: re-add requireAuth / requireRole('Admin', 'Manager') on write routes once a login system exists and issues JWTs with a role claim.` Routes: `GET /`, `GET /stats`, `POST /import`, `GET /:id`, `POST /`, `PUT /:id`, `DELETE /:id`.

```js
async function assertScheduleMatchesLift(scheduleId, liftId) {
```

```js
import axios from 'axios';
```

- frontend/src/features/lift-workflow/steps/RectificationsStep.jsx:24-26

gates Add/Edit/Delete buttons, DataGrid Actions column, CSV import button, advance-status buttons. Purely client-side UX gate today (no backend enforcement currently, that's what we're adding). `App.jsx` renders user.name/user.role in a header avatar (no role-check there).

`EndorseButton.jsx` — no role check at all currently, comment explicitly defers role-gating to "once auth/roles exist... gated to an EM-staff role".

Backend test convention: Jest + Supertest + mongodb-memory-server, per-student folders `backend/tests/<Name>/`, real example is `backend/tests/Ryan/rectification.test.js` — build a minimal `express()` app mounting only the router under test (never require server.js directly), duplicate the error-handling middleware inline, beforeAll spins up MongoMemoryServer + mongoose.connect, afterAll disconnects+stops, afterEach does Model.deleteMany({}) per model touched, helper factories like createDefect/createLift with overridable defaults. package.json has per-student scripts (test:ryan etc.), no umbrella "run all" script. ## Task spec (exact target behavior — do not reinterpret, this is final)

Three roles: Master, Admin, Staff (explicitly NO Contractor role, and NO "Manager" role — that label must be fully retired from every check, replaced with a proper 3-way role check per the matrix below, not a straight find-replace):

- **Master**: creates any account (Admin or Staff). Full CRUD on Schedules, Inspections, Defects, Rectifications, plus Endorse.
- **Admin**: creates Staff accounts only (cannot create Admin or Master). Full CRUD on Schedules (create+assign to Staff), full CRUD + full visibility on Inspections/Defects/Rectifications across every staff member, plus Endorse.
- **Staff**: cannot manage any accounts.
  - Schedules: read-only, ONLY schedules assigned to them, EXCEPT they CAN update just the `status` field on their own assigned schedules. Cannot create/delete/edit any other field (date, lift company, town council, reassignment).
  - Inspections: can create/edit, but only for a schedule assigned to them (or no schedule link at all, if currently allowed).
  - Defects: can log freely, not restricted to lifts/schedules assigned to them.
  - Rectifications: can create/submit. CANNOT call endorse under any circumstance (Admin/Master only).

### Backend requirements
1. New User model `backend/src/models/users/User.js`: name, email (unique), passwordHash, role (enum Master/Admin/Staff), createdBy (ref User), isDeleted (soft delete per cascadeDelete.js pattern), timestamps.
2. Auth: bcrypt password hashing, JWT sessions. POST /api/auth/login (email+password -> JWT with role+userId claims). Account management endpoints: create/list/deactivate users, gated server-side by account-creation rules (Master creates anyone, Admin creates Staff only) — not just hidden in UI.
3. Middleware: requireAuth + requireRole(...roles), wired into ALL FIVE route files listed above (including scheduling, which currently has zero auth mentions). Rectifications' PATCH /:id/endorse requires Admin or Master specifically (stricter than the router's general write-gate).
4. Schedule model: add assignedStaffId (ObjectId ref User, nullable) as real relational link (assignedInspector stays as free-text snapshot, no longer source of truth for access control). Migration/backfill step mapping existing assignedInspector strings to real User accounts where confidently matchable, else null.
5. Query scoping: listSchedules filters to assignedStaffId=req.user._id for Staff role (Admin/Master unfiltered). updateSchedule rejects any Staff-submitted field other than status, and rejects entirely if schedule not assigned to that Staff user. createInspection additionally verifies (for Staff caller) that referenced schedule's assignedStaffId matches caller's own id — extends (doesn't replace) assertScheduleMatchesLift.

### Frontend requirements
1. Replace AuthContext.jsx hardcoded dev user with real login: login page, JWT in localStorage, Authorization header on every API call, logout action.
2. Update all 5 `canEdit` checks to reflect real 3-role matrix instead of flat binary — e.g. SchedulingStep.jsx "Add Schedule" button + full-field edit should be Admin/Master only, but Staff needs a separate affordance to update just status on their own assigned schedules (not the same old canEdit flag reused).
3. EndorseButton.jsx renders only for Admin/Master.
4. New account management screen: Master sees/creates Admin+Staff; Admin sees/creates Staff only; UI enforcement only, backend is real guard.
5. SchedulingStep.jsx / Lift Workflow schedule list auto-filters to "assigned to me" for Staff role in the UI (cosmetic, since backend already scopes the query) — avoid implying they could see more (e.g. no "all schedules" toggle/link shown to Staff).

### Testing requirements
Backend tests covering: Staff cannot create/delete a schedule (403); Staff can update only status on their own assigned schedule; Staff cannot touch a schedule assigned to someone else; Staff cannot call endorse endpoint; Admin cannot create another Admin account (only Master can).

### Explicitly out of scope
No Contractor/lift-company-facing role or portal.

A concrete, mechanical implementation plan covering:
1. Exact User model schema (field types, validators, indexes — e.g. unique index on email).
2. Exact JWT payload shape, expiry, secret handling (env var, fallback/dev behavior), and where token verification lives.
3. Exact middleware module design: file path(s) under a new backend/src/middleware/ dir, requireAuth signature, requireRole signature, how they attach req.user, how they interact with asyncHandler, and exact error codes/messages via ApiError.unauthorized/forbidden.
4. Exact auth routes/controller: file paths, POST /api/auth/login flow, account management endpoints (paths, methods, request/response shapes, which roles can hit which).
5. Exact per-route-file middleware wiring for all 5 resource routers — which routes get requireAuth only vs requireAuth+requireRole(...), and exact role lists per route given the matrix above (be precise about scheduling's create/update/delete, inspections' create scoping, rectifications' endorse route, defects being unrestricted-by-assignment but still requiring auth).
6. Exact Schedule model diff + migration/backfill approach (where the backfill code lives, how "confident match" is defined — e.g. exact case-insensitive name equality with a uniqueness check among Users with role Staff — and what happens on ambiguous/no match).
7. Exact controller-level logic changes for listSchedules, updateSchedule, createInspection (pseudocode-level detail, not full code, but precise about what fields/branches change).
8. Exact frontend plan: AuthContext redesign (state shape, login()/logout() methods, token persistence, initial-load token validation/decoding), client.js interceptor design, new Login page location/route, new account-management page location/route + routing changes needed (check if react-router-dom routes are defined in App.jsx or a router file — flag this as something to verify during implementation if not already known), exact replacement logic for each of the 5 canEdit sites (what new variables/flags each file needs, e.g. `canManageSchedule`, `canUpdateOwnStatus`, `canEditFull` etc.), EndorseButton.jsx change, and how Staff-only "assigned to me" filtering surfaces in SchedulingStep.jsx.
9. Exact new test file plan: which files, what each test does, what fixtures/helper factories are needed (createUser factory, JWT-signing helper for auth headers in supertest requests).
10. A safe, ordered rollout plan (what order to build things in so the app isn't broken mid-way, e.g. backend auth infra -> migration -> route gating -> frontend login -> frontend gating -> tests), and a list of risks/edge cases to flag (e.g. existing seeded data with no matching user breaking Staff schedule visibility, JWT secret missing in .env, CORS/localStorage token expiry handling, what happens to in-flight sessions when isDeleted is set on a user).

Be decisive — pick one approach per open question rather than presenting multiple options. This app is a student/small-team project (see repo conventions above), so favor simplicity and consistency with existing patterns over enterprise-grade complexity (e.g. no refresh-token rotation, no rate limiting infra needed, plain JWT with reasonable expiry like 8h is fine).

## 1. User Model — exact schema

New file: `backend/src/models/users/User.js`

```js
const mongoose = require('mongoose');
const ROLES = ['Master', 'Admin', 'Staff'];

const userSchema = new mongoose.Schema({
  name:         { type: String, required: true, trim: true },
  email:        { type: String, required: true, unique: true, trim: true, lowercase: true },
  passwordHash: { type: String, required: true },
  role:         { type: String, required: true, enum: ROLES },
  createdBy:    { type: mongoose.Schema.Types.ObjectId, ref: 'User', default: null },
  isDeleted:    { type: Boolean, default: false },
}, { timestamps: true });

userSchema.index({ role: 1 }); // Admin's account list and Staff-scoping lookups both filter by role

module.exports = mongoose.model('User', userSchema);
module.exports.ROLES = ROLES;
```

- `unique: true` on `email` is the same pattern `Lift.liftCode` already uses — no separate `.index()` call needed for it.
- `lowercase: true` + `trim: true` on email so login lookups are case-insensitive without extra query logic.
- `passwordHash` never `select: false` — this app has no field-level projection convention anywhere else (controllers already return full docs via `ok(res, doc)`), so keep it consistent; just make sure `authController` never spreads the raw Mongoose doc back into a response — always hand-build `{ id, name, email, role }` response shapes (see §4).
- No unique index needed on `name` — display-only.
- bcrypt salt rounds: **10** (standard default, `bcryptjs`).

Add to `backend/package.json` dependencies: `"bcryptjs": "^2.4.3"`, `"jsonwebtoken": "^9.0.2"`.

## 2. JWT payload, expiry, secret handling

New file: `backend/src/utils/jwt.js` — single place both the auth controller (signing) and the middleware (verifying) import from, so the payload shape only exists in one place.

```js
const jwt = require('jsonwebtoken');

function signToken(user) {
  return jwt.sign(
    { userId: String(user._id), role: user.role, name: user.name, email: user.email },
    process.env.JWT_SECRET,
    { expiresIn: '8h' }
  );
}

function verifyToken(token) {
  return jwt.verify(token, process.env.JWT_SECRET); // throws on invalid/expired
}

module.exports = { signToken, verifyToken };
```

**Exact payload shape:** `{ userId, role, name, email, iat, exp }` (`iat`/`exp` added automatically by `jsonwebtoken`).

**Expiry:** `8h` flat string, no refresh token, no rotation (matches the "keep it simple" directive).

**Secret handling — decisive, no silent fallback:** at the very top of `backend/src/server.js`, right after `require('dotenv').config()`, add a fail-fast guard:

```js
if (!process.env.JWT_SECRET) {
  console.error('FATAL: JWT_SECRET is not set. Add it to backend/.env before starting the server.');
  process.exit(1);
}
```

No `'dev-secret'` default — a guessable fallback is worse than a loud crash for a project that has an already-populated `.env.example` placeholder. Document this explicitly in `.env.example`'s existing `JWT_SECRET=` line comment.

**Where verification lives:** exclusively inside `requireAuth` in the new middleware module (§3) — no other file calls `jwt.verify` directly.

---

## 3. Middleware module design

New directory: `backend/src/middleware/`
New file: `backend/src/middleware/auth.js`

```js
const ApiError = require('../utils/ApiError');
const asyncHandler = require('../utils/asyncHandler');
const { verifyToken } = require('../utils/jwt');
const User = require('../models/users/User');

// requireAuth: verifies the Bearer token AND re-checks the user still exists / isn't
// deactivated on every request (not just at login) — this is what makes deactivating an
// account (isDeleted: true) take effect on the user's very next call instead of waiting
// out the 8h token expiry.
const requireAuth = asyncHandler(async (req, res, next) => {
  const header = req.headers.authorization || '';
  const [scheme, token] = header.split(' ');
  if (scheme !== 'Bearer' || !token) {
    throw ApiError.unauthorized('Missing or invalid Authorization header');
  }

  let payload;
  try {
    payload = verifyToken(token);
  } catch (err) {
    throw ApiError.unauthorized('Invalid or expired token');
  }

  const user = await User.findOne({ _id: payload.userId, isDeleted: false }).catch(() => null);
  if (!user) throw ApiError.unauthorized('Account no longer exists or has been deactivated');

  req.user = { _id: user._id, name: user.name, email: user.email, role: user.role };
  next();
});

// requireRole(...roles): synchronous, no DB access, no asyncHandler needed — Express 4
// auto-forwards synchronous throws inside middleware to the error handler, same as any
// synchronous controller code already in this repo.
function requireRole(...roles) {
  return function (req, res, next) {
    if (!req.user) throw ApiError.unauthorized();
    if (!roles.includes(req.user.role)) {
      throw ApiError.forbidden(`This action requires role: ${roles.join(' or ')}`);
    }
    next();
  };
}

module.exports = { requireAuth, requireRole };
```

- `requireAuth` MUST be wrapped in `asyncHandler` (it does an async `User.findOne`); `requireRole(...)` does not need it (purely synchronous).
- Both reuse `ApiError.unauthorized`/`ApiError.forbidden` exactly as they exist today — no new error shapes.
- Route usage pattern (Express supports chained middlewares per route): `router.post('/', requireAuth, requireRole('Admin', 'Master'), createSchedule);`
- `req.user` shape is always `{ _id, name, email, role }` — every downstream controller change in §7 reads `req.user._id` / `req.user.role`.

## 4. Auth routes/controller — exact paths, flows, request/response shapes

New files:
- `backend/src/models/users/User.js` (§1)
- `backend/src/controllers/auth/authController.js`
- `backend/src/routes/auth/authRoutes.js`

Mount in `backend/src/server.js`, added alongside the other five `app.use('/api/...')` lines (before the global error handler):
```js

```

### Route table (`authRoutes.js`)

| Method | Path | Middleware | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/auth/login` | none (public) | email+password → token |
| GET | `/api/auth/me` | `requireAuth` | returns caller's own profile — this is what the frontend uses on initial load instead of client-side JWT decoding |
| POST | `/api/auth/users` | `requireAuth` (role check done **inside the controller**, not `requireRole`, because the allowed target role depends on the caller's role — see below) | create account |
| GET | `/api/auth/users` | `requireAuth`, `requireRole('Master', 'Admin')` | list accounts, controller filters by caller role |
| PATCH | `/api/auth/users/:id/deactivate` | `requireAuth`, `requireRole('Master', 'Admin')` | soft-delete (`isDeleted: true`), controller enforces scoping + self-deactivation guard |

### `POST /api/auth/login`
Request: `{ email, password }`.
Flow: find `User` by `email.toLowerCase()` with `isDeleted: false` → if not found, `ApiError.unauthorized('Invalid email or password')` (never reveal which field was wrong) → `bcrypt.compare(password, user.passwordHash)` → if false, same generic 401 message → `signToken(user)` → respond via `ok(res, { token, user: { id: user._id, name: user.name, email: user.email, role: user.role } }, 'Login successful')`.

### `GET /api/auth/me`
Flow: `req.user` is already populated by `requireAuth` — just `ok(res, req.user)`. No extra DB call needed (requireAuth already did the fresh lookup this request).

### `POST /api/auth/users` (create account)
Request: `{ name, email, password, role }`.
Flow (all inside controller, using `req.user.role` from `requireAuth`):
```
if (req.user.role === 'Staff') throw ApiError.forbidden('Staff cannot create accounts');
if (req.user.role === 'Admin' && role !== 'Staff') throw ApiError.forbidden('Admin can only create Staff accounts');
// Master: role may be 'Admin' or 'Staff' — reject role === 'Master' outright (no one, not even
// Master, creates another Master through this endpoint; treat Master accounts as pre-provisioned)
if (role === 'Master') throw ApiError.forbidden('Master accounts cannot be created through this endpoint');
if (!ROLES.includes(role)) throw ApiError.badRequest(`role must be one of ${ROLES.join(', ')}`);
// standard required-field + duplicate-email checks (mirror assertRequiredFields pattern used elsewhere)
const passwordHash = await bcrypt.hash(password, 10);
const user = await User.create({ name, email: email.toLowerCase(), passwordHash, role, createdBy: req.user._id });
ok(res, { id: user._id, name: user.name, email: user.email, role: user.role }, 'Account created', 201);
```

### `GET /api/auth/users` (list accounts)
Flow: `requireRole('Master','Admin')` already blocks Staff. Then:
```
const filter = { isDeleted: false };
if (req.user.role === 'Admin') filter.role = 'Staff'; // Admin only ever sees Staff accounts, not Master/Admin
const users = await User.find(filter, 'name email role createdBy createdAt').sort({ name: 1 });
ok(res, users);
```

### `PATCH /api/auth/users/:id/deactivate`
Flow: `requireRole('Master','Admin')`, then:
```
if (String(req.params.id) === String(req.user._id)) throw ApiError.badRequest('Cannot deactivate your own account');
const target = await User.findOne({ _id: req.params.id, isDeleted: false });
if (!target) throw ApiError.notFound('Account not found');
if (req.user.role === 'Admin' && target.role !== 'Staff') throw ApiError.forbidden('Admin can only deactivate Staff accounts');
target.isDeleted = true;
await target.save();
ok(res, { id: target._id }, 'Account deactivated');
```

### Migration/backfill — decisive placement: **standalone script**, not seed.js

New file: `backend/scripts/migrateAssignedStaff.js`. New package.json script: `"migrate:assigned-staff": "node scripts/migrateAssignedStaff.js"`.

**Why a standalone script and not folded into `seed.js`:** `seed.js`'s entire pattern is destructive (`Model.deleteMany({}); Model.insertMany(...)`) — it's meant to wipe and repopulate a dev DB from scratch. The backfill's job is the opposite: run once, non-destructively, against whatever `Schedule`/`User` documents already exist in a real/shared dev database, to set a field on existing documents without touching anything else. Mixing that "repair pass" semantics into a wipe-and-reseed script is exactly the kind of foot-gun `cleanupOrphans()` was already kept separate to avoid (it's dead code specifically because nobody wired it into an automatic path) — same reasoning applies here, so `migrateAssignedStaff.js` follows the `cleanupOrphans()` precedent: a plain Node script, connects to `DATABASE_URL` itself, run manually via `npm run migrate:assigned-staff`, safe to re-run (idempotent — re-running only touches schedules that still have `assignedStaffId: null`).

**Exact "confident match" definition:**
```js
async function backfillAssignedStaffId() {
  const staff = await User.find({ role: 'Staff', isDeleted: false });
  const schedules = await Schedule.find({ assignedStaffId: null, assignedInspector: { $ne: '' }, isDeleted: false });

  let matched = 0, ambiguous = 0, noMatch = 0;
  for (const schedule of schedules) {
    const name = schedule.assignedInspector.trim().toLowerCase();
    const candidates = staff.filter((u) => u.name.trim().toLowerCase() === name);
    if (candidates.length === 1) {
      schedule.assignedStaffId = candidates[0]._id;
      await schedule.save();
      matched += 1;
    } else if (candidates.length > 1) {
      ambiguous += 1;
      console.warn(`Ambiguous match for "${schedule.assignedInspector}" (schedule ${schedule._id}) — ${candidates.length} Staff users share that name. Left null.`);
    } else {
      noMatch += 1;
      console.warn(`No Staff user found matching "${schedule.assignedInspector}" (schedule ${schedule._id}). Left null.`);
    }
  }
  console.log(`Backfill done: ${matched} matched, ${ambiguous} ambiguous, ${noMatch} no match.`);
}
```
Rule, stated plainly: **exact case-insensitive name equality** (`.trim().toLowerCase()`) against `User` documents with `role: 'Staff'` and `isDeleted: false`. Exactly one hit → set it. Zero or more than one hit → leave `assignedStaffId: null` and log a warning; no fuzzy/partial matching under any circumstance. Schedules left `null` after this run are still visible to Admin/Master (unrestricted) and simply invisible to every Staff user until an Admin/Master manually re-assigns them via the existing full-field `PUT /:id` (Admin/Master already get unrestricted field access there).

### `schedulingController.js` — `getSchedule` (recommended addition beyond literal spec — flagged)
The spec only calls out `listSchedules`/`updateSchedule`, but without this, a Staff user could `GET /api/scheduling/<any-id>` directly and read a schedule not assigned to them, even though the list view hides it — a direct-object-reference gap. Recommend closing it:
```
async function getSchedule(req, res) {
  const schedule = await Schedule.findOne({ _id: req.params.id, isDeleted: false });
  if (!schedule) throw ApiError.notFound(...);
  if (req.user.role === 'Staff' && String(schedule.assignedStaffId) !== String(req.user._id)) {
    throw ApiError.notFound('Schedule not found'); // 404, not 403 — don't reveal existence
  }
  ok(res, schedule);
```

### `schedulingController.js` — `createSchedule`
No body changes needed — route-level `requireRole('Admin','Master')` already keeps Staff out entirely. Optionally accept `assignedStaffId` in the destructured body fields (alongside `assignedInspector`) so Admin/Master can set the real link at creation time, not just via a later edit.

### `schedulingController.js` — `updateSchedule` — the core change
```
async function updateSchedule(req, res) {
  const existing = await Schedule.findOne({ _id: req.params.id, isDeleted: false });
  if (!existing) throw ApiError.notFound(...);

  let updates;
  if (req.user.role === 'Staff') {
    if (String(existing.assignedStaffId) !== String(req.user._id)) {
      throw ApiError.notFound('Schedule not found'); // not assigned to this Staff user — 404, don't leak existence
    }
    const disallowedKeys = Object.keys(req.body).filter((k) => k !== 'status');
    if (disallowedKeys.length) {
      throw ApiError.forbidden(`Staff can only update the status field (rejected: ${disallowedKeys.join(', ')})`);
    }
    updates = { status: req.body.status };
  } else {
    updates = { ...req.body }; // Admin/Master: full-field update, unchanged from today
  }

  if (updates.status && !Schedule.STATUS_VALUES.includes(updates.status)) {
    throw ApiError.badRequest(...);
  }

  const schedule = await Schedule.findOneAndUpdate({ _id: req.params.id, isDeleted: false }, updates, { new: true, runValidators: true });
  ok(res, schedule);
}
```
**Note on error style:** this controller currently uses raw `try/catch` + `res.status(...).json({error})`, not the `asyncHandler`/`ApiError` pattern the newer controllers (inspections, rectifications, defects) use. Recommend converting `schedulingController.js` to the `asyncHandler` + `ApiError` pattern as part of this change (it's touched anyway) so its error shape (`{success:false,message}`) matches every other module instead of `{error: '...'}` — this is a small but real inconsistency the frontend's `err.response?.data?.message` reads currently won't pick up from this controller today.

### `inspectionController.js` — `createInspection`
Add one new assertion, reusing the already-fetched `schedule`, right after `assertScheduleMatchesLift`:
```
async function assertScheduleMatchesLift(scheduleId, liftId) {
  if (!scheduleId) return null;
  const schedule = await Schedule.findOne({ _id: scheduleId, isDeleted: false }).catch(() => null);
  if (!schedule) throw ApiError.badRequest('Selected schedule not found');
  if (schedule.liftId && String(schedule.liftId) !== String(liftId)) throw ApiError.badRequest('Selected schedule is for a different lift');

    throw ApiError.forbidden('You can only create an inspection against a schedule assigned to you');

}

const createInspection = asyncHandler(async (req, res) => {
  assertRequiredFields(req.body);
  assertNotFutureDate(req.body.inspectionDate);
```

## 8. Frontend plan

### AuthContext redesign — `frontend/src/context/AuthContext.jsx`
State shape:
```js
{ user: { id, name, email, role } | null, isLoading: boolean, login(email, password), logout() }
```
- Token storage key: `localStorage` key `'emservices_token'` (pick this exact literal, used identically in `client.js`'s interceptor).
- On mount (`useEffect` in `AuthProvider`): read the token; if present, call `authApi.me()` (hits `GET /api/auth/me`, which `client.js`'s interceptor already attaches the token to — see below) to get a **fresh** profile rather than decoding the JWT client-side (this also catches a since-deactivated account immediately instead of trusting a stale decoded payload). On success, `setUser(...)`. On failure (401), clear the token and leave `user: null`. `isLoading` is `true` until this resolves either way.
- `login(email, password)`: calls `authApi.login(email, password)` → on success, `localStorage.setItem('emservices_token', token)`, `setUser(user)`, return; on failure, propagate the error so `LoginPage` can show it.
- `logout()`: `localStorage.removeItem('emservices_token')`, `setUser(null)`. No server call (plain JWT, no revocation list, per the "no refresh-token rotation" simplicity directive).
- Default context value (used only if `useAuth()` is somehow called outside the provider): `{ user: null, isLoading: true, login: async () => {}, logout: () => {} }` — no more hardcoded `Dev User`/`Admin`.

### `client.js` interceptor design — `frontend/src/api/client.js`
```js
client.interceptors.request.use((config) => {
  const token = localStorage.getItem('emservices_token');
  if (token) config.headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${token}`;
  return config;
});

client.interceptors.response.use(
  (res) => res,
  (err) => {
    if (err.response?.status === 401) {
      localStorage.removeItem('emservices_token');
      window.location.assign('/'); // hard reload — AuthContext re-initializes clean, LoginPage renders
    }
    return Promise.reject(err);
  }
);
```
Deliberately no pub/sub/event-bus for the 401 case — a hard reload is simpler and acceptable at this app's scale (flagged as a tradeoff: any unsaved in-page state is lost on forced logout).

### Routing — verified, not assumed
Confirmed: `main.jsx` wraps everything in `<BrowserRouter>`, but **`App.jsx` contains no `<Routes>`/`<Route>` elements at all** — it derives the active tab manually from `useLocation().pathname` and `Workspace.jsx` picks a component out of a plain `FEATURE_PAGES` object keyed by tab id. There is no real react-router route tree to hook a `/login` path into.

Decisive approach — don't introduce a `<Routes>` tree (inconsistent with the existing manual-tab-switch convention, and higher risk of breaking existing deep-links like `/lifts`, `/lift-workflow`):
- New file `frontend/src/AuthGate.jsx`: reads `useAuth()`; if `isLoading`, render a minimal centered spinner; if no `user`, render `<LoginPage />` (standalone, no AppBar/TabBar chrome); otherwise render `<App />`.
- `main.jsx` changes its render tree from `<AuthProvider><App /></AuthProvider>` to `<AuthProvider><AuthGate /></AuthProvider>`.
- New file `frontend/src/features/auth/LoginPage.jsx` — simple centered card with email/password fields, calls `login(email, password)` from `useAuth()`, shows the error message on failure, no routing needed (it just is what's rendered when `user` is `null`).

## 10. Rollout order + risks/edge cases

### Ordered rollout (each phase leaves the app in a working state before the next begins)

1. **Backend auth infra (non-breaking, additive only).** Add `bcryptjs`/`jsonwebtoken` deps; `User` model; `utils/jwt.js`; `middleware/auth.js`; `authController.js` + `authRoutes.js`; mount `/api/auth` in `server.js`; add the `JWT_SECRET` fail-fast check. Nothing else changes — every existing route stays open, the app is fully functional throughout, `/api/auth/*` exists standalone and is independently testable.
2. **Schedule model diff.** Add `assignedStaffId` + index — purely additive/nullable, non-breaking.
3. **`seed.js` changes.** Add `seedUsers()`, wire `assignedStaffId` directly into `buildSampleSchedules`. Run `npm run seed` to refresh local/dev data with real users and real links.
4. **`migrateAssignedStaff.js`.** Write the standalone script (for any pre-existing shared dev DB data outside the fresh reseed — likely a no-op for this project if `seed.js` is genuinely the only data source, but still implement it since it's explicitly requested and is good practice regardless).
5. **Backend route gating (the breaking change).** Wire `requireAuth`/`requireRole` into all five resource routers, plus the controller-level scoping logic in `schedulingController.js` and `inspectionController.js`. Do this as one atomic change (not gradually) — a half-gated set of routers is a confusing intermediate state. **In the same change**, update the five existing per-student test files (`tests/Ryan`, `tests/Aeric`, `tests/Javier`, `tests/Elijah`, `tests/Lucio`) to attach a valid `Authorization` header via the new shared `testAuthHelper.js` — every request in those files currently sends none, so they will all start failing the instant `requireAuth` lands on their routers. This is a hard cross-cutting dependency, not optional cleanup — flag it to the team early.
6. **Frontend `AuthContext` + `client.js` interceptor + `LoginPage` + `AuthGate`.** Must follow *immediately* after phase 5 (not before) — deploying phase 5 without this leaves the frontend's old hardcoded `Dev User` sending zero `Authorization` headers, so every API call in the app would start 401ing.
7. **Frontend gating.** `utils/roles.js`, the five `canEdit`-site rewrites, `EndorseButton.jsx`, `AccountsPage.jsx` + `TABS`/`FEATURE_PAGES` wiring.
8. **New `tests/Auth/` suite** + `testAuthHelper.js` (can actually be written in parallel with phase 5, but only runs green once phase 5 lands).
9. **Manual smoke test + docs.** Log in as each seeded role, walk through the matrix by hand; update `.env.example`'s `JWT_SECRET=` comment and note the seeded dev credentials somewhere discoverable (README or the `seedUsers()` console output already covers this).

### Risks / edge cases to flag explicitly

- **Orphaned schedules after migration/backfill:** any `Schedule` whose `assignedInspector` doesn't exactly (case-insensitively) match exactly one `User.name` with `role: 'Staff'` ends up with `assignedStaffId: null` — invisible to every Staff user, visible only to Admin/Master until manually reassigned. The seed-data path avoids this by construction (matching names deliberately); the migration-script path for any other existing data does not, and needs a manual admin pass afterward.
- **`JWT_SECRET` missing:** deliberate fail-fast crash on server boot, not a silent insecure default — document clearly so it doesn't read as a mysterious startup failure.
- **Token expiry + no refresh:** on expiry, the next API call 401s, the response interceptor clears storage and reloads to `LoginPage`. Acceptable per the explicit "no refresh-token rotation" instruction, but means a user mid-form-entry loses that work on expiry — not solved here, flagged only.

## 2. JWT payload, expiry, secret handling

New file: `backend/src/utils/jwt.js` — single place both the auth controller (signing) and the middleware (verifying) import from, so the payload shape only exists in one place.

```js
const jwt = require('jsonwebtoken');

function signToken(user) {
  return jwt.sign(
    { userId: String(user._id), role: user.role, name: user.name, email: user.email },
    process.env.JWT_SECRET,
    { expiresIn: '8h' }
  );
}

function verifyToken(token) {
  return jwt.verify(token, process.env.JWT_SECRET); // throws on invalid/expired
}

module.exports = { signToken, verifyToken };
```

**Exact payload shape:** `{ userId, role, name, email, iat, exp }` (`iat`/`exp` added automatically by `jsonwebtoken`).

**Expiry:** `8h` flat string, no refresh token, no rotation (matches the "keep it simple" directive).

**Secret handling — decisive, no silent fallback:** at the very top of `backend/src/server.js`, right after `require('dotenv').config()`, add a fail-fast guard:

```js
if (!process.env.JWT_SECRET) {
  console.error('FATAL: JWT_SECRET is not set. Add it to backend/.env before starting the server.');
  process.exit(1);
}
```

No `'dev-secret'` default — a guessable fallback is worse than a loud crash for a project that has an already-populated `.env.example` placeholder. Document this explicitly in `.env.example`'s existing `JWT_SECRET=` line comment.

## 3. Middleware module design

New directory: `backend/src/middleware/`
New file: `backend/src/middleware/auth.js`

```js
const ApiError = require('../utils/ApiError');
const asyncHandler = require('../utils/asyncHandler');
const { verifyToken } = require('../utils/jwt');
const User = require('../models/users/User');

// requireAuth: verifies the Bearer token AND re-checks the user still exists / isn't
// deactivated on every request (not just at login) — this is what makes deactivating an
// account (isDeleted: true) take effect on the user's very next call instead of waiting
// out the 8h token expiry.
const requireAuth = asyncHandler(async (req, res, next) => {
  const header = req.headers.authorization || '';
  const [scheme, token] = header.split(' ');
  if (scheme !== 'Bearer' || !token) {
    throw ApiError.unauthorized('Missing or invalid Authorization header');
  }

  let payload;
  try {
    payload = verifyToken(token);
  } catch (err) {
    throw ApiError.unauthorized('Invalid or expired token');
  }

  const user = await User.findOne({ _id: payload.userId, isDeleted: false }).catch(() => null);
  if (!user) throw ApiError.unauthorized('Account no longer exists or has been deactivated');

  req.user = { _id: user._id, name: user.name, email: user.email, role: user.role };
  next();
});

// requireRole(...roles): synchronous, no DB access, no asyncHandler needed — Express 4
// auto-forwards synchronous throws inside middleware to the error handler, same as any
// synchronous controller code already in this repo.
function requireRole(...roles) {
  return function (req, res, next) {
    if (!req.user) throw ApiError.unauthorized();
    if (!roles.includes(req.user.role)) {
      throw ApiError.forbidden(`This action requires role: ${roles.join(' or ')}`);
    }
    next();
  };
}

module.exports = { requireAuth, requireRole };
```

- `requireAuth` MUST be wrapped in `asyncHandler` (it does an async `User.findOne`); `requireRole(...)` does not need it (purely synchronous).
- Both reuse `ApiError.unauthorized`/`ApiError.forbidden` exactly as they exist today — no new error shapes.
- Route usage pattern (Express supports chained middlewares per route): `router.post('/', requireAuth, requireRole('Admin', 'Master'), createSchedule);`
- `req.user` shape is always `{ _id, name, email, role }` — every downstream controller change in §7 reads `req.user._id` / `req.user.role`.

| Method | Path | Middleware | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/auth/login` | none (public) | email+password → token |
| GET | `/api/auth/me` | `requireAuth` | returns caller's own profile — this is what the frontend uses on initial load instead of client-side JWT decoding |
| POST | `/api/auth/users` | `requireAuth` (role check done **inside the controller**, not `requireRole`, because the allowed target role depends on the caller's role — see below) | create account |

### `POST /api/auth/login`
Request: `{ email, password }`.
Flow: find `User` by `email.toLowerCase()` with `isDeleted: false` → if not found, `ApiError.unauthorized('Invalid email or password')` (never reveal which field was wrong) → `bcrypt.compare(password, user.passwordHash)` → if false, same generic 401 message → `signToken(user)` → respond via `ok(res, { token, user: { id: user._id, name: user.name, email: user.email, role: user.role } }, 'Login successful')`.

### `GET /api/auth/me`
Flow: `req.user` is already populated by `requireAuth` — just `ok(res, req.user)`. No extra DB call needed (requireAuth already did the fresh lookup this request).

### `POST /api/auth/users` (create account)

Flow (all inside controller, using `req.user.role` from `requireAuth`):
```

if (req.user.role === 'Admin' && role !== 'Staff') throw ApiError.forbidden('Admin can only create Staff accounts');

const user = await User.create({ name, email: email.toLowerCase(), passwordHash, role, createdBy: req.user._id });
```

Flow: `requireRole('Master','Admin')` already blocks Staff. Then:

```
if (req.user.role === 'Admin') filter.role = 'Staff'; // Admin only ever sees Staff accounts, not Master/Admin
```

Flow: `requireRole('Master','Admin')`, then:

### Migration/backfill — decisive placement: **standalone script**, not seed.js

New file: `backend/scripts/migrateAssignedStaff.js`. New package.json script: `"migrate:assigned-staff": "node scripts/migrateAssignedStaff.js"`.

**Why a standalone script and not folded into `seed.js`:** `seed.js`'s entire pattern is destructive (`Model.deleteMany({}); Model.insertMany(...)`) — it's meant to wipe and repopulate a dev DB from scratch. The backfill's job is the opposite: run once, non-destructively, against whatever `Schedule`/`User` documents already exist in a real/shared dev database, to set a field on existing documents without touching anything else. Mixing that "repair pass" semantics into a wipe-and-reseed script is exactly the kind of foot-gun `cleanupOrphans()` was already kept separate to avoid (it's dead code specifically because nobody wired it into an automatic path) — same reasoning applies here, so `migrateAssignedStaff.js` follows the `cleanupOrphans()` precedent: a plain Node script, connects to `DATABASE_URL` itself, run manually via `npm run migrate:assigned-staff`, safe to re-run (idempotent — re-running only touches schedules that still have `assignedStaffId: null`).

**Exact "confident match" definition:**
```js
async function backfillAssignedStaffId() {
  const staff = await User.find({ role: 'Staff', isDeleted: false });
  const schedules = await Schedule.find({ assignedStaffId: null, assignedInspector: { $ne: '' }, isDeleted: false });

  let matched = 0, ambiguous = 0, noMatch = 0;
  for (const schedule of schedules) {
    const name = schedule.assignedInspector.trim().toLowerCase();
    const candidates = staff.filter((u) => u.name.trim().toLowerCase() === name);
    if (candidates.length === 1) {
      schedule.assignedStaffId = candidates[0]._id;
      await schedule.save();
      matched += 1;
    } else if (candidates.length > 1) {
      ambiguous += 1;
      console.warn(`Ambiguous match for "${schedule.assignedInspector}" (schedule ${schedule._id}) — ${candidates.length} Staff users share that name. Left null.`);
    } else {
      noMatch += 1;
      console.warn(`No Staff user found matching "${schedule.assignedInspector}" (schedule ${schedule._id}). Left null.`);
    }
  }
  console.log(`Backfill done: ${matched} matched, ${ambiguous} ambiguous, ${noMatch} no match.`);
}
```
Rule, stated plainly: **exact case-insensitive name equality** (`.trim().toLowerCase()`) against `User` documents with `role: 'Staff'` and `isDeleted: false`. Exactly one hit → set it. Zero or more than one hit → leave `assignedStaffId: null` and log a warning; no fuzzy/partial matching under any circumstance. Schedules left `null` after this run are still visible to Admin/Master (unrestricted) and simply invisible to every Staff user until an Admin/Master manually re-assigns them via the existing full-field `PUT /:id` (Admin/Master already get unrestricted field access there).

### `schedulingController.js` — `updateSchedule` — the core change
```
async function updateSchedule(req, res) {
  const existing = await Schedule.findOne({ _id: req.params.id, isDeleted: false });
  if (!existing) throw ApiError.notFound(...);

  let updates;
  if (req.user.role === 'Staff') {
    if (String(existing.assignedStaffId) !== String(req.user._id)) {
      throw ApiError.notFound('Schedule not found'); // not assigned to this Staff user — 404, don't leak existence
    }
    const disallowedKeys = Object.keys(req.body).filter((k) => k !== 'status');
    if (disallowedKeys.length) {
      throw ApiError.forbidden(`Staff can only update the status field (rejected: ${disallowedKeys.join(', ')})`);
    }
    updates = { status: req.body.status };
  } else {
    updates = { ...req.body }; // Admin/Master: full-field update, unchanged from today
  }

  if (updates.status && !Schedule.STATUS_VALUES.includes(updates.status)) {
    throw ApiError.badRequest(...);
  }

  const schedule = await Schedule.findOneAndUpdate({ _id: req.params.id, isDeleted: false }, updates, { new: true, runValidators: true });
  ok(res, schedule);
}
```
**Note on error style:** this controller currently uses raw `try/catch` + `res.status(...).json({error})`, not the `asyncHandler`/`ApiError` pattern the newer controllers (inspections, rectifications, defects) use. Recommend converting `schedulingController.js` to the `asyncHandler` + `ApiError` pattern as part of this change (it's touched anyway) so its error shape (`{success:false,message}`) matches every other module instead of `{error: '...'}` — this is a small but real inconsistency the frontend's `err.response?.data?.message` reads currently won't pick up from this controller today.

```
  if (schedule.liftId && String(schedule.liftId) !== String(liftId)) throw ApiError.badRequest('Selected schedule is for a different lift');
  return schedule; // CHANGED: now returns the schedule instead of nothing, so callers can reuse it
}

function assertScheduleAssignedToStaff(schedule, user) {
  if (user.role !== 'Staff') return; // only enforced for Staff callers
  if (!schedule) return; // no schedule link at all — still allowed per spec ("or no schedule link at all")
  if (String(schedule.assignedStaffId) !== String(user._id)) {
    throw ApiError.forbidden('You can only create an inspection against a schedule assigned to you');
  }
}

const createInspection = asyncHandler(async (req, res) => {
  assertRequiredFields(req.body);
  assertNotFutureDate(req.body.inspectionDate);
  const reportNo = await nextReportNo();
  const { liftCode, block } = await resolveLiftSnapshot(req.body.liftId);
  const schedule = await assertScheduleMatchesLift(req.body.scheduleId, req.body.liftId);
  assertScheduleAssignedToStaff(schedule, req.user);
  ...rest unchanged...
});
```

**Recommended symmetric extension (flagged, beyond literal spec text):** `updateInspection` currently re-validates the schedule link ("Re-validate the schedule link whenever either side of it changes") but doesn't check assignment. Recommend applying the same `assertScheduleAssignedToStaff` check there too, using the already-resolved `effectiveLiftId`/effective `scheduleId` in that block — otherwise a Staff user could create an inspection tied to their own schedule, then edit it while it's still Draft to switch `scheduleId` to someone else's schedule, since `updateInspection`'s existing scope check only validates lift-consistency, not ownership. Confirm with reviewer since it's not explicitly called for in the spec, but it closes an obvious loophole in the exact mechanism the spec does ask for on create.

### `rectificationController.js`
No controller body changes needed at all — `createRectification`/`updateRectification` stay exactly as-is (Staff is allowed full access per the matrix), and `endorseRectification`'s protection is entirely the route-level `requireRole('Admin','Master')` added in §5. No controller-level role branching required here.

### `defectController.js`
No controller body changes — defects are explicitly unrestricted-by-assignment; only the route-level `requireAuth` (and `requireRole` on delete) from §5 apply.

## 8. Frontend plan

### AuthContext redesign — `frontend/src/context/AuthContext.jsx`
State shape:
```js
{ user: { id, name, email, role } | null, isLoading: boolean, login(email, password), logout() }
```
- Token storage key: `localStorage` key `'emservices_token'` (pick this exact literal, used identically in `client.js`'s interceptor).
- On mount (`useEffect` in `AuthProvider`): read the token; if present, call `authApi.me()` (hits `GET /api/auth/me`, which `client.js`'s interceptor already attaches the token to — see below) to get a **fresh** profile rather than decoding the JWT client-side (this also catches a since-deactivated account immediately instead of trusting a stale decoded payload). On success, `setUser(...)`. On failure (401), clear the token and leave `user: null`. `isLoading` is `true` until this resolves either way.
- `login(email, password)`: calls `authApi.login(email, password)` → on success, `localStorage.setItem('emservices_token', token)`, `setUser(user)`, return; on failure, propagate the error so `LoginPage` can show it.
- `logout()`: `localStorage.removeItem('emservices_token')`, `setUser(null)`. No server call (plain JWT, no revocation list, per the "no refresh-token rotation" simplicity directive).
- Default context value (used only if `useAuth()` is somehow called outside the provider): `{ user: null, isLoading: true, login: async () => {}, logout: () => {} }` — no more hardcoded `Dev User`/`Admin`.

### `client.js` interceptor design — `frontend/src/api/client.js`
```js
client.interceptors.request.use((config) => {
  const token = localStorage.getItem('emservices_token');
  if (token) config.headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${token}`;
  return config;
});

client.interceptors.response.use(
  (res) => res,
  (err) => {
    if (err.response?.status === 401) {
      localStorage.removeItem('emservices_token');
      window.location.assign('/'); // hard reload — AuthContext re-initializes clean, LoginPage renders
    }
    return Promise.reject(err);
  }
);
```
Deliberately no pub/sub/event-bus for the 401 case — a hard reload is simpler and acceptable at this app's scale (flagged as a tradeoff: any unsaved in-page state is lost on forced logout).

### Routing — verified, not assumed
Confirmed: `main.jsx` wraps everything in `<BrowserRouter>`, but **`App.jsx` contains no `<Routes>`/`<Route>` elements at all** — it derives the active tab manually from `useLocation().pathname` and `Workspace.jsx` picks a component out of a plain `FEATURE_PAGES` object keyed by tab id. There is no real react-router route tree to hook a `/login` path into.

Decisive approach — don't introduce a `<Routes>` tree (inconsistent with the existing manual-tab-switch convention, and higher risk of breaking existing deep-links like `/lifts`, `/lift-workflow`):
- New file `frontend/src/AuthGate.jsx`: reads `useAuth()`; if `isLoading`, render a minimal centered spinner; if no `user`, render `<LoginPage />` (standalone, no AppBar/TabBar chrome); otherwise render `<App />`.
- `main.jsx` changes its render tree from `<AuthProvider><App /></AuthProvider>` to `<AuthProvider><AuthGate /></AuthProvider>`.
- New file `frontend/src/features/auth/LoginPage.jsx` — simple centered card with email/password fields, calls `login(email, password)` from `useAuth()`, shows the error message on failure, no routing needed (it just is what's rendered when `user` is `null`).

### New account-management page
- New files: `frontend/src/features/accounts/AccountsPage.jsx`, `frontend/src/features/accounts/AccountFormDialog.jsx`, `frontend/src/api/authApi.js` (exports `login`, `me`, `listUsers`, `createUser`, `deactivateUser`, all thin wrappers around `client`).
- `App.jsx`: change the static exported `TABS` array to a `getVisibleTabs(role)` helper (or filter inline) that appends `{ id: 'accounts', label: 'Accounts' }` only when `user.role === 'Master' || user.role === 'Admin'`. Both `App.jsx` (for `TabBar`) and any other tab consumer must use this same helper so a Staff user never even sees the tab.
- `Workspace.jsx`: add `accounts: AccountsPage` to `FEATURE_PAGES`. For defense-in-depth against a Staff user manually navigating to `/accounts` in the URL bar, `AccountsPage.jsx` itself should also check `useAuth().user.role` at the top and render an "Unauthorized" placeholder if it's `'Staff'`, rather than relying solely on the tab being hidden.
- Inside `AccountsPage.jsx`: fetch via `authApi.listUsers()` (already server-filtered per §4 — Admin only ever gets Staff back), render a simple table/DataGrid + "Add Account" button. The create dialog's role `<Select>` options are also client-filtered (`Master` sees `Admin`/`Staff`; `Admin` sees `Staff` only) purely for UX — the real enforcement is server-side per §4.

### New shared role helper — `frontend/src/utils/roles.js`
```js
export const ROLES = { MASTER: 'Master', ADMIN: 'Admin', STAFF: 'Staff' };
export const isAdminOrMaster = (role) => role === ROLES.ADMIN || role === ROLES.MASTER;
```
This is what makes the 5-site change a genuine 3-way redesign rather than a find-replace of `'Manager'` → something else: every file below imports `isAdminOrMaster` (or checks `role === ROLES.STAFF` directly) instead of hand-rolling the old two-role string comparison, and `'Manager'` is fully deleted from the codebase.

### Exact per-file replacement

**`frontend/src/features/lifts/Lifts.jsx:55-57`**
```js
const canEdit = isAdminOrMaster(user.role);
```
No new Staff affordance — matrix grants Staff nothing on Lifts.

**`frontend/src/features/lift-workflow/steps/InspectionsStep.jsx:55-57`**
Staff can create/edit (scoped server-side), so the flag needs to split:
```js
const canCreateOrEdit = true; // all 3 authenticated roles per matrix — server enforces schedule-ownership scoping for Staff
const canManageFull = isAdminOrMaster(user.role); // gates delete / notify-contractor-triggering UI
```
Replace the old single `canEdit` usage: Add/Edit buttons now check `canCreateOrEdit` (effectively always shown), Delete button and any "Notify Contractor" action check `canManageFull`.

**`frontend/src/features/lift-workflow/steps/DefectsStep.jsx:25-27`**
```js
const canCreateOrEdit = true; // defects are unrestricted-by-assignment for all roles
const canManageFull = isAdminOrMaster(user.role); // gates delete only
```

**`frontend/src/features/lift-workflow/steps/RectificationsStep.jsx:24-26`**
```js
const canCreateOrEdit = true; // create/submit allowed for all 3 roles
const canManageFull = isAdminOrMaster(user.role); // gates delete only; Endorse is handled inside EndorseButton.jsx itself, not here
```

**`frontend/src/features/lift-workflow/steps/SchedulingStep.jsx:28-30`** — most involved change:
```js
const canManageSchedule = isAdminOrMaster(user.role); // Add Schedule button, full-field Edit, Delete
const canUpdateOwnStatus = user.role === ROLES.STAFF;  // separate, narrower affordance
const isOwnSchedule = (row) => String(row.assignedStaffId) === String(user.id);
```
- `"Add Schedule"` button (currently `{canEdit && (...)}`) → `{canManageSchedule && (...)}`.
- Actions column `width`: `canManageSchedule ? 190 : 70` (was `canEdit ? 190 : 70`).
- Actions column render: Edit/Delete icons stay gated on `canManageSchedule` only. The "advance status" arrow button changes from `{canEdit && NEXT_STATUS[...] && (...)}` to:
  ```jsx
  {(canManageSchedule || (canUpdateOwnStatus && isOwnSchedule(params.row))) && NEXT_STATUS[params.row.status] && (
    <IconButton onClick={() => handleAdvanceStatus(params.row)}>...</IconButton>
  )}
  ```
  `handleAdvanceStatus` already calls `scheduleApi.updateSchedule(schedule._id, { status: nextStatus })` — a single-key body — which is exactly what the new backend `updateSchedule` allows a Staff caller to send, so no change needed to that function itself.
- **"Assigned to me" cosmetic filtering (§ requirement 5):** since backend `listSchedules` already scopes to `assignedStaffId` for Staff (§7), `scheduleApi.fetchSchedules()` naturally returns only the caller's own schedules for a Staff user — **no extra client-side filter code is needed or should be added**. The only action item here is a *negative* one: do not add any "view all schedules" toggle/link visible to Staff (none currently exists, so this is a constraint on future changes, not a code diff).

### `EndorseButton.jsx`
Currently receives only `{ rectification, onEndorse }` — no `user` prop. Import `useAuth` and `isAdminOrMaster` directly inside the component itself (matches how every other file already imports `useAuth` locally rather than prop-drilling):
```jsx
import { useAuth } from '../../context/AuthContext';
import { isAdminOrMaster } from '../../utils/roles';
...
export default function EndorseButton({ rectification, onEndorse }) {
  const { user } = useAuth();
  ...
  if (rectification.status !== 'Submitted') return null;
  if (!isAdminOrMaster(user.role)) return null; // NEW — was previously ungated entirely
  ...
}
```

---

## 9. New test file plan

New folder: `backend/tests/Auth/` (generic name since the implementing developer's identity is unknown — matches the existing per-student folder convention, e.g. `tests/Ryan/`) containing `auth.test.js` and `test-cases.md`. New package.json script: `"test:auth": "jest tests/Auth --runInBand"`.

Also add a **shared** helper (not per-folder duplicated) since every existing student's test file is about to need one:
New file: `backend/tests/testAuthHelper.js`
```js
const bcrypt = require('bcryptjs');
const jwt = require('jsonwebtoken');
const User = require('../src/models/users/User');

async function createTestUser(role, overrides = {}) {
  const passwordHash = await bcrypt.hash('Passw0rd!', 10);
  return User.create({ name: `Test ${role}`, email: `${role.toLowerCase()}-${Date.now()}@test.local`, passwordHash, role, ...overrides });
}

function authHeader(user) {
  const token = jwt.sign({ userId: String(user._id), role: user.role, name: user.name, email: user.email }, process.env.JWT_SECRET, { expiresIn: '8h' });
  return `Bearer ${token}`;
}

module.exports = { createTestUser, authHeader };
```
(Every test file's `beforeAll` must set `process.env.JWT_SECRET = 'test-secret'` before requiring anything that reads it, e.g. at the very top of the file, since the middleware reads it at request time not at import time.)

### `backend/tests/Auth/auth.test.js` — `buildApp()` mounts `authRoutes`, `schedulingRoutes`, and `rectificationsRoutes` together (all three needed to cover the required scenarios) plus the same inline error-handling middleware as `tests/Ryan/rectification.test.js`. `beforeEach`/`afterEach` clears `User`, `Schedule`, `Rectification`, `Defect` collections.

Test cases (mirroring the exact "Testing requirements" list):
1. `POST /api/auth/login` — wrong password → 401; happy path → 200 + `data.token` + `data.user.role`.
2. `requireAuth` — no `Authorization` header on a protected route → 401; malformed header (`"Bearer"` with no token, or wrong scheme) → 401; tampered/invalid token → 401.
3. `POST /api/scheduling` as Staff → 403 (role-gated at route level, never reaches controller).
4. `DELETE /api/scheduling/:id` as Staff → 403.
5. `PUT /api/scheduling/:id` as Staff on their **own** assigned schedule with body `{ status: 'In Progress' }` → 200, and the returned doc's other fields (e.g. `townCouncil`) are unchanged.
6. `PUT /api/scheduling/:id` as Staff on their own schedule with body `{ status: 'In Progress', townCouncil: 'Someone Else TC' }` (extra field) → 403 with a message naming the rejected field.
7. `PUT /api/scheduling/:id` as Staff on a schedule assigned to a **different** Staff user → 404 (per the "don't leak existence" choice in §7).
8. `PATCH /api/rectifications/:id/endorse` as Staff (on a `Submitted` rectification) → 403, never reaches the controller's own status-transition logic.
9. `POST /api/auth/users` as Admin with `role: 'Admin'` in the body → 403 ("Admin can only create Staff accounts").
10. `POST /api/auth/users` as Admin with `role: 'Staff'` → 201 (positive control case, proves the 403 above is role-specific, not blanket-denied).
11. `POST /api/auth/users` as Master with `role: 'Admin'` → 201 (positive case — Master can create Admin).
12. `POST /api/auth/users` with `role: 'Master'` (from either caller) → 403 ("Master accounts cannot be created through this endpoint").

`test-cases.md` documents each of the above in prose, following the same format as `tests/Ryan/test-cases.md`.

---

## 10. Rollout order + risks/edge cases

### Ordered rollout (each phase leaves the app in a working state before the next begins)

1. **Backend auth infra (non-breaking, additive only).** Add `bcryptjs`/`jsonwebtoken` deps; `User` model; `utils/jwt.js`; `middleware/auth.js`; `authController.js` + `authRoutes.js`; mount `/api/auth` in `server.js`; add the `JWT_SECRET` fail-fast check. Nothing else changes — every existing route stays open, the app is fully functional throughout, `/api/auth/*` exists standalone and is independently testable.
2. **Schedule model diff.** Add `assignedStaffId` + index — purely additive/nullable, non-breaking.
3. **`seed.js` changes.** Add `seedUsers()`, wire `assignedStaffId` directly into `buildSampleSchedules`. Run `npm run seed` to refresh local/dev data with real users and real links.
4. **`migrateAssignedStaff.js`.** Write the standalone script (for any pre-existing shared dev DB data outside the fresh reseed — likely a no-op for this project if `seed.js` is genuinely the only data source, but still implement it since it's explicitly requested and is good practice regardless).
5. **Backend route gating (the breaking change).** Wire `requireAuth`/`requireRole` into all five resource routers, plus the controller-level scoping logic in `schedulingController.js` and `inspectionController.js`. Do this as one atomic change (not gradually) — a half-gated set of routers is a confusing intermediate state. **In the same change**, update the five existing per-student test files (`tests/Ryan`, `tests/Aeric`, `tests/Javier`, `tests/Elijah`, `tests/Lucio`) to attach a valid `Authorization` header via the new shared `testAuthHelper.js` — every request in those files currently sends none, so they will all start failing the instant `requireAuth` lands on their routers. This is a hard cross-cutting dependency, not optional cleanup — flag it to the team early.
6. **Frontend `AuthContext` + `client.js` interceptor + `LoginPage` + `AuthGate`.** Must follow *immediately* after phase 5 (not before) — deploying phase 5 without this leaves the frontend's old hardcoded `Dev User` sending zero `Authorization` headers, so every API call in the app would start 401ing.
7. **Frontend gating.** `utils/roles.js`, the five `canEdit`-site rewrites, `EndorseButton.jsx`, `AccountsPage.jsx` + `TABS`/`FEATURE_PAGES` wiring.
8. **New `tests/Auth/` suite** + `testAuthHelper.js` (can actually be written in parallel with phase 5, but only runs green once phase 5 lands).
9. **Manual smoke test + docs.** Log in as each seeded role, walk through the matrix by hand; update `.env.example`'s `JWT_SECRET=` comment and note the seeded dev credentials somewhere discoverable (README or the `seedUsers()` console output already covers this).

### Risks / edge cases to flag explicitly

- **Orphaned schedules after migration/backfill:** any `Schedule` whose `assignedInspector` doesn't exactly (case-insensitively) match exactly one `User.name` with `role: 'Staff'` ends up with `assignedStaffId: null` — invisible to every Staff user, visible only to Admin/Master until manually reassigned. The seed-data path avoids this by construction (matching names deliberately); the migration-script path for any other existing data does not, and needs a manual admin pass afterward.
- **`JWT_SECRET` missing:** deliberate fail-fast crash on server boot, not a silent insecure default — document clearly so it doesn't read as a mysterious startup failure.
- **Token expiry + no refresh:** on expiry, the next API call 401s, the response interceptor clears storage and reloads to `LoginPage`. Acceptable per the explicit "no refresh-token rotation" instruction, but means a user mid-form-entry loses that work on expiry — not solved here, flagged only.
- **Deactivation takes effect immediately, not at next login:** because `requireAuth` re-queries `User` (`isDeleted: false`) on every request rather than trusting the token's claims, a deactivated user is locked out on their very next call even with 7+ hours left on their token — this is the deliberate answer to "what happens to in-flight sessions."
- **CORS:** `server.js` already does bare `app.use(cors())` (reflects all origins/headers by default) — the `Authorization` header should pass through without extra config, but worth a manual check once the frontend interceptor is live.
- **Losing the dev bypass:** once phase 5+6 ship together, there is no more "everyone is Admin" dev shortcut — anyone running the app locally needs a seeded login (`seedUsers()`'s console output is the intended source of truth for this).
- **Self-lockout guards:** `deactivateUser` rejects an actor deactivating their own account; a "last remaining Master" guard is deliberately **not** implemented (out of scope for this project's size) — flagged as an accepted gap, not an oversight.
- **Scope discipline — don't over-restrict:** Inspections/Defects/Rectifications `list`/`get` endpoints are **not** scoped to "created by me" or "assigned to me" for Staff anywhere in this spec — only `Schedules` get that treatment, and only `createInspection`'s schedule-link gets an ownership check. It would be an easy, over-eager mistake during implementation to also filter `listInspections`/`listDefects`/`listRectifications` by the caller — the spec explicitly does not ask for that (Defects are "not restricted to lifts/schedules assigned to them" and Rectifications/Inspections lists aren't mentioned as scoped at all), so implementers should resist adding it.
- **Two additions beyond literal spec text, flagged for reviewer sign-off before implementing:** (a) ownership check added to `getSchedule` (GET `/:id`), and (b) the same `assertScheduleAssignedToStaff` check extended into `updateInspection`, not just `createInspection`. Both close obvious direct-object-reference / edit-after-create loopholes in the exact mechanisms the spec does ask for, but neither is explicitly named in the task spec — confirm before building.

- `backend/src/middleware/auth.js` (new — requireAuth/requireRole, the mechanism every other change hangs off)
- `backend/src/models/users/User.js` (new — User schema, role enum, referenced by Schedule.assignedStaffId and every controller's req.user)

- `frontend/src/context/AuthContext.jsx` (full redesign — everything frontend-side depends on this shape)
- `backend/seed.js` (seedUsers() + assignedStaffId wiring — makes the whole RBAC matrix testable locally)</result>
