# User Management + RBAC (Master/Admin/Staff)

## Context

The app currently has zero real auth: `AuthContext.jsx` hardcodes every user as `{name:'Dev User', role:'Admin'}`, no backend route checks anything, and five route files carry a standing `TODO: re-add requireAuth / requireRole('Admin','Manager')...` comment (scheduling has no such TODO at all — it was missed). This pass replaces that with real login (bcrypt+JWT), a proper 3-role model (Master/Admin/Staff — "Manager" is retired entirely), server-side enforcement of who can do what, and a real relational link (`assignedStaffId`) between Schedules and Staff instead of the free-text `assignedInspector` string. Frontend `canEdit` binary checks (7 sites) get replaced with per-role logic matching the real matrix.

All paths below are relative to `em-services-lift-servicing/` (the actual repo root one level under the folder name).

## Role matrix (final, confirmed)

| | Master | Admin | Staff |
|---|---|---|---|
| Create accounts | Admin or Staff | Staff only | none |
| Schedules | full CRUD | full CRUD, assign to Staff | read-only, own schedules only; can PATCH `status` only |
| Inspections | full CRUD | full CRUD, all staff | create/edit own-schedule (or no-schedule) inspections only |
| Inspections: notify-contractor / delete | yes | yes | **no** (confirmed: Admin/Master only — Staff notifies contractors manually outside the app) |
| Defects | full CRUD | full CRUD | create/edit freely (unrestricted by assignment); **delete is Admin/Master only** |
| Rectifications | full CRUD + Endorse | full CRUD + Endorse | create/submit only; **cannot endorse, cannot delete** |

Two gap-closing additions confirmed with user (beyond literal spec wording, now in scope):
- `GET /api/scheduling/:id` gets the same Staff-ownership check as the list endpoint (404 if not assigned to them).
- `updateInspection` gets the same `assertScheduleAssignedToStaff` check as `createInspection` (prevents a Staff user re-pointing an existing inspection at someone else's schedule).

## Backend

### 1. User model — `backend/src/models/users/User.js` (new)
`name` (String, required), `email` (String, required, unique, trim, lowercase), `passwordHash` (String, required), `role` (enum `['Master','Admin','Staff']`, required), `createdBy` (ObjectId ref User, default null), `isDeleted` (Boolean, default false), timestamps. Index on `role`. Export `ROLES` alongside the model (pattern: `module.exports.ROLES = ROLES`).

### 2. Auth utils/middleware
- `backend/src/utils/jwt.js` (new): `signToken(user)` → `jwt.sign({userId, role, name, email}, process.env.JWT_SECRET, {expiresIn:'8h'})`; `verifyToken(token)` → `jwt.verify(...)`. Single source of truth for payload shape.
- `backend/src/middleware/auth.js` (new dir): `requireAuth` (wrapped in `asyncHandler`) — parses `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, verifies it, **re-fetches the User by id with `isDeleted:false` on every request** (so deactivation takes effect immediately, not at token expiry), sets `req.user = {_id, name, email, role}`, else throws `ApiError.unauthorized(...)`. `requireRole(...roles)` — plain sync middleware, throws `ApiError.forbidden(...)` if `req.user.role` isn't in the list. Reuse existing `ApiError.unauthorized`/`.forbidden` factories — no new error shapes.
- `backend/server.js`: add a fail-fast guard right after `dotenv.config()` — `if (!process.env.JWT_SECRET) { console.error(...); process.exit(1); }`. No insecure fallback default.
- Add `bcryptjs` and `jsonwebtoken` to `backend/package.json`.

### 3. Auth routes/controller — `backend/src/controllers/auth/authController.js`, `backend/src/routes/auth/authRoutes.js` (new), mounted as `/api/auth` in `server.js`

| Method | Path | Middleware | Behavior |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/login` | none | email+password → bcrypt compare → JWT + `{id,name,email,role}`. Generic "Invalid email or password" on any failure (don't leak which field). |
| GET | `/me` | requireAuth | returns `req.user` as-is (already a fresh lookup) |
| POST | `/users` | requireAuth | create account; role-eligibility checked **inside controller** (depends on caller's role): Staff → 403; Admin creating non-Staff → 403; anyone creating `role:'Master'` → 403 ("Master accounts cannot be created through this endpoint"); else bcrypt-hash password, `createdBy: req.user._id` |
| GET | `/users` | requireAuth, requireRole('Master','Admin') | list accounts; Admin's filter forces `role:'Staff'` only, Master sees Admin+Staff |
| PATCH | `/users/:id/deactivate` | requireAuth, requireRole('Master','Admin') | soft-delete; reject self-deactivation; Admin can only deactivate Staff targets |

### 4. Route-file middleware wiring (all 5 resource routers gain `requireAuth` on every route; `requireRole` added where matrix narrows it)

- **liftRoutes.js**: replace TODO. Write routes (`POST /import`, `POST /`, `PUT /:id`, `DELETE /:id`) → `requireRole('Admin','Master')`. Reads → `requireAuth` only.
- **defectsRoutes.js**: replace TODO. `POST /`, `PUT /:id` → `requireAuth` only (all 3 roles). `DELETE /:id` → add `requireRole('Admin','Master')`.
- **inspectionsRoutes.js**: replace TODO. `POST /`, `PUT /:id` → `requireAuth` only (ownership enforced in controller, see §5). `PATCH /:id/notify-contractor` and `DELETE /:id` → `requireRole('Admin','Master')` (confirmed).
- **rectificationsRoutes.js**: replace TODO (it's the one that explicitly calls out endorse). `POST /`, `PUT /:id` → `requireAuth` only. `PATCH /:id/endorse` → `requireRole('Admin','Master')`. `DELETE /:id` → `requireRole('Admin','Master')`.
- **schedulingRoutes.js**: currently has zero auth mentions — add fresh. `GET /`, `GET /:id`, `PUT /:id` → `requireAuth` only (scoping done in controller). `POST /`, `DELETE /:id` → `requireRole('Admin','Master')`.

### 5. Schedule model — `backend/src/models/scheduling/Schedule.js`
Add `assignedStaffId: {type: ObjectId, ref:'User', default:null}` + `scheduleSchema.index({assignedStaffId:1})`. `assignedInspector` stays as-is (display snapshot only, no longer read for access control).

**Convert `schedulingController.js` to the `asyncHandler`/`ApiError` pattern while touched** — it currently uses raw try/catch + `res.status().json({error})` unlike every other controller; that inconsistency is what's blocking the frontend's `err.response?.data?.message` reads from this module today, so bring it in line as part of this change (confirmed via direct read of the file, matches design-agent's flag).

Controller changes:
- **listSchedules**: add `if (req.user.role === 'Staff') filter.assignedStaffId = req.user._id;` (Admin/Master unfiltered).
- **getSchedule**: after fetch, `if (req.user.role==='Staff' && String(schedule.assignedStaffId)!==String(req.user._id)) throw ApiError.notFound(...)` (confirmed addition — 404 not 403, don't leak existence).
- **updateSchedule**: fetch existing first. If `req.user.role==='Staff'`: reject (404) if not their schedule; reject (403, naming the field) if body has any key other than `status`; else apply `{status}` only. Admin/Master: full-body update as today. Keep existing `STATUS_VALUES` validation.
- **createSchedule**: no logic change — route-level `requireRole('Admin','Master')` already excludes Staff. Optionally accept `assignedStaffId` in the body alongside `assignedInspector`.

### 6. Migration/backfill — standalone script, not folded into seed.js
New file `backend/scripts/migrateAssignedStaff.js` + `package.json` script `"migrate:assigned-staff": "node scripts/migrateAssignedStaff.js"`. Rationale: `seed.js` is destructive (wipe+reseed); this must be a non-destructive, idempotent repair pass — same reasoning that kept `cleanupOrphans()` (in `cascadeDelete.js`) as a separate, manually-run function rather than wired into an automatic path.

Matching rule: for each `Schedule` with `assignedStaffId: null` and non-empty `assignedInspector`, case-insensitive trimmed exact-name match against `User` docs where `role:'Staff', isDeleted:false`. Exactly one hit → set `assignedStaffId`. Zero or multiple hits → leave `null`, log a warning (no fuzzy matching, ever). Log a summary count (matched/ambiguous/no-match) at the end.

### 7. seed.js changes
Add `seedUsers()` (same `deleteMany`+`insertMany` shape as every other seed function), called before schedules. Seed Staff user names to **exactly match** existing `assignedInspector` strings already in `buildSampleSchedules` (e.g. `Jessica S.`, `Marcus T.`, `Jane Lim`, `John Tan`) so the schedule-building step can set `assignedStaffId` directly via a `byName` lookup map — guaranteed correct linkage for seed data, no reliance on the migration script for the fresh-seed path. Print seeded dev credentials (email/plaintext password) to console for local login. Also seed one Master and one Admin account.

### 8. Inspections controller — `backend/src/controllers/inspections/inspectionController.js`
- `assertScheduleMatchesLift` now **returns** the fetched `schedule` (was previously void) so callers can reuse it without a second query.
- New `assertScheduleAssignedToStaff(schedule, user)`: no-op unless `user.role==='Staff'`; no-op if `schedule` is null (no-schedule-link case still allowed per spec); else throws `ApiError.forbidden(...)` if `schedule.assignedStaffId` doesn't match `user._id`.
- `createInspection`: call `assertScheduleAssignedToStaff(schedule, req.user)` right after `assertScheduleMatchesLift`.
- `updateInspection`: apply the same `assertScheduleAssignedToStaff` check wherever it currently re-validates the schedule/lift link on edit (confirmed addition — closes the re-point-to-someone-else's-schedule loophole).

### 9. Rectifications / Defects controllers
No controller-body changes. Rectifications' `endorseRectification` is protected purely by the route-level `requireRole('Admin','Master')` (§4). Defects need no ownership logic per spec (unrestricted by assignment); only route-level gating applies.

## Frontend

### 1. `AuthContext.jsx` — full redesign
State: `{user: {id,name,email,role}|null, isLoading, login(email,password), logout()}`. Token key: `localStorage['emservices_token']`. On mount, if a token exists, call `GET /api/auth/me` (via the interceptor below) to get a **fresh** profile rather than client-decoding the JWT — catches deactivation immediately. `login()` stores token + sets user or throws for the login page to display. `logout()` clears token + user, no server call needed (plain JWT, no revocation).

### 2. `frontend/src/api/client.js`
Request interceptor attaches `Authorization: Bearer <token>` from localStorage when present. Response interceptor: on 401, clear the token and hard-reload (`window.location.assign('/')`) so `AuthContext` reinitializes clean into the login page.

### 3. Routing
Confirmed `App.jsx` has no `<Routes>` tree (manual tab-switch via `Workspace.jsx`'s `FEATURE_PAGES`) — don't introduce react-router routes. New `frontend/src/AuthGate.jsx`: renders a spinner while `isLoading`, `<LoginPage/>` if no user, else `<App/>`. `main.jsx` wraps `<AuthProvider><AuthGate/></AuthProvider>`. New `frontend/src/features/auth/LoginPage.jsx` (standalone card, no chrome).

### 4. Shared role helper — `frontend/src/utils/roles.js` (new)
`ROLES = {MASTER,ADMIN,STAFF}`, `isAdminOrMaster(role)`. Every one of the 5 sites below imports this instead of hand-rolling a two-role string check — this is what makes it a real 3-way redesign, not a find-replace of "Manager".

### 5. The 5 `canEdit` sites
- **Lifts.jsx**: `canEdit = isAdminOrMaster(user.role)` (Staff gets nothing here — matrix grants none).
- **InspectionsStep.jsx**: split into `canCreateOrEdit = true` (server scopes Staff) and `canManageFull = isAdminOrMaster(user.role)` gating notify-contractor + delete.
- **DefectsStep.jsx**: `canCreateOrEdit = true`, `canManageFull = isAdminOrMaster(user.role)` gating delete only.
- **RectificationsStep.jsx**: `canCreateOrEdit = true`, `canManageFull = isAdminOrMaster(user.role)` gating delete only (Endorse handled inside `EndorseButton.jsx` itself).
- **SchedulingStep.jsx** (most involved): `canManageSchedule = isAdminOrMaster(user.role)` (Add/Edit-full/Delete), `canUpdateOwnStatus = user.role===ROLES.STAFF` + `isOwnSchedule(row)` helper gating just the advance-status action, which already calls `updateSchedule(id, {status})` — a single-key body, exactly what the new backend allows for Staff. No client-side "assigned to me" filter needed — backend already scopes the list; the only rule is *not* adding any "view all" toggle visible to Staff.

### 6. `EndorseButton.jsx`
Import `useAuth`/`isAdminOrMaster` directly in the component; `if (!isAdminOrMaster(user.role)) return null;` alongside the existing `status!=='Submitted'` check.

### 7. Account management screen
New `frontend/src/features/accounts/AccountsPage.jsx` + `AccountFormDialog.jsx`, new `frontend/src/api/authApi.js` (login/me/listUsers/createUser/deactivateUser wrappers). `App.jsx`'s tab list adds an "Accounts" tab only for Master/Admin; `Workspace.jsx` maps it to `AccountsPage`. `AccountsPage.jsx` itself also role-checks at the top (defense in depth against manual navigation) — list/create options are server-filtered already (§3 backend) so the UI just reflects what the API returns.

## Tests

New `backend/tests/Auth/` (generic name, matches existing per-student folder convention) with `auth.test.js` + `test-cases.md`, plus a shared `backend/tests/testAuthHelper.js` (`createTestUser(role, overrides)`, `authHeader(user)` for signing a test JWT). New `package.json` script `"test:auth"`.

Cases: login wrong-password (401) / happy path (200+token); `requireAuth` missing/malformed/invalid token (401); Staff `POST /api/scheduling` (403); Staff `DELETE /api/scheduling/:id` (403); Staff `PUT` own schedule with `{status}` only (200, other fields unchanged); Staff `PUT` own schedule with an extra field (403, names the rejected field); Staff `PUT` a schedule assigned to someone else (404); Staff `PATCH /:id/endorse` (403); Admin `POST /api/auth/users` with `role:'Admin'` (403) and with `role:'Staff'` (201, positive control); Master `POST /api/auth/users` with `role:'Admin'` (201); anyone posting `role:'Master'` (403).

**Cross-cutting note, flagged for the team**: the five existing per-student test files (`tests/Ryan`, `tests/Aeric`, `tests/Javier`, `tests/Elijah`, `tests/Lucio`) send zero `Authorization` headers today — the moment `requireAuth` lands on their routers, all of them start failing. They must be updated (via the new `testAuthHelper.js`) in the same change that adds route gating, not as separate cleanup.

## Rollout order (each step leaves the app working)
1. Backend auth infra only (User model, jwt util, middleware, `/api/auth/*` mounted) — additive, nothing else changes yet.
2. Schedule model diff (`assignedStaffId` + index) — additive/nullable.
3. `seed.js` changes, run `npm run seed` to get real linked dev data.
4. `migrateAssignedStaff.js` script (for any data outside the fresh reseed).
5. Route gating across all 5 resource routers + scheduling/inspection controller scoping, **together with** updating the 5 existing test files to send auth headers — one atomic change.
6. Frontend `AuthContext`/`client.js` interceptor/`LoginPage`/`AuthGate` — must land immediately after step 5 (old hardcoded dev user sends no token → everything 401s otherwise).
7. Frontend `canEdit` site rewrites, `EndorseButton.jsx`, `AccountsPage.jsx`.
8. New `tests/Auth/` suite.
9. Manual smoke test logging in as each seeded role.

## Verification
- `npm test` (backend) across all per-student suites + new `test:auth` — must pass with route gating live.
- `npm run seed` then manually log in via the new login page as the seeded Master, Admin, and each Staff user; confirm: Staff sees only their own schedules and can move status but not edit other fields; Admin/Master see everything; EndorseButton only renders for Admin/Master; Accounts tab only visible to Admin/Master with correct create-role restrictions.
- Confirm server refuses to boot without `JWT_SECRET` set.

## Context

The app currently has zero real auth: `AuthContext.jsx` hardcodes every user as `{name:'Dev User', role:'Admin'}`, no backend route checks anything, and five route files carry a standing `TODO: re-add requireAuth / requireRole('Admin','Manager')...` comment (scheduling has no such TODO at all — it was missed). This pass replaces that with real login (bcrypt+JWT), a proper 3-role model (Master/Admin/Staff — "Manager" is retired entirely), server-side enforcement of who can do what, and a real relational link (`assignedStaffId`) between Schedules and Staff instead of the free-text `assignedInspector` string. Frontend `canEdit` binary checks (7 sites) get replaced with per-role logic matching the real matrix.

All paths below are relative to `em-services-lift-servicing/` (the actual repo root one level under the folder name).

## Role matrix (final, confirmed)

| | Master | Admin | Staff |
|---|---|---|---|
| Create accounts | Admin or Staff | Staff only | none |
| Schedules | full CRUD | full CRUD, assign to Staff | read-only, own schedules only; can PATCH `status` only |
| Inspections | full CRUD | full CRUD, all staff | create/edit own-schedule (or no-schedule) inspections only |
| Inspections: notify-contractor / delete | yes | yes | **no** (confirmed: Admin/Master only — Staff notifies contractors manually outside the app) |
| Defects | full CRUD | full CRUD | create/edit freely (unrestricted by assignment); **delete is Admin/Master only** |
| Rectifications | full CRUD + Endorse | full CRUD + Endorse | create/submit only; **cannot endorse, cannot delete** |

Two gap-closing additions confirmed with user (beyond literal spec wording, now in scope):
- `GET /api/scheduling/:id` gets the same Staff-ownership check as the list endpoint (404 if not assigned to them).
- `updateInspection` gets the same `assertScheduleAssignedToStaff` check as `createInspection` (prevents a Staff user re-pointing an existing inspection at someone else's schedule).

### 1. User model — `backend/src/models/users/User.js` (new)
`name` (String, required), `email` (String, required, unique, trim, lowercase), `passwordHash` (String, required), `role` (enum `['Master','Admin','Staff']`, required), `createdBy` (ObjectId ref User, default null), `isDeleted` (Boolean, default false), timestamps. 1	const mongoose = require('mongoose');
2	
3	// Matches the client's paper spot-check form fields (Town Council / Lift Company /
4	// Block-Lift Address) so a schedule entry can stand alone even before the Lifts
5	// feature's own model/collection exists. Once Lifts is built, `liftId` can be
6	// populated to link back to the canonical lift record.
7	const STATUS_VALUES = ['Scheduled', 'Assigned', 'In Progress', 'Completed', 'Cancelled'];
8	
9	const scheduleSchema = new mongoose.Schema(
10	  {
11	    townCouncil: { type: String, required: true, trim: true },
12	    liftCompany: { type: String, required: true, trim: true },
13	    blockAddress: { type: String, required: true, trim: true },
14	
15	    // Optional forward link to the Lifts feature's model.
16	    liftId: { type: mongoose.Schema.Types.ObjectId, ref: 'Lift', default: null },
17	
18	    scheduledDate: { type: Date, required: true },
19	    assignedInspector: { type: String, trim: true, default: '' },
20	
21	    status: {
22	      type: String,
23	      enum: STATUS_VALUES,
24	      default: 'Scheduled',
25	    },
26	
27	    notes: { type: String, trim: true, default: '' },
28	
29	    // Soft delete, per assignment guide (delete can be optional/soft).
30	    isDeleted: { type: Boolean, default: false },
31	  },
32	  { timestamps: true }
33	);
34	
35	scheduleSchema.index({ scheduledDate: 1 });
36	scheduleSchema.index({ status: 1 });
37	
38	const Schedule = mongoose.model('Schedule', scheduleSchema);
39	Schedule.STATUS_VALUES = STATUS_VALUES;
40	
41	module.exports = Schedule;

# Backend Test Cases — User Management / RBAC

Feature owner: Auth (User Management + RBAC pass)
Automated in: `auth.test.js` (Jest + Supertest, against an in-memory MongoDB via
`mongodb-memory-server` — no real Atlas connection needed to run these). The test file mounts
`authRoutes`, `schedulingRoutes` and `rectificationsRoutes` together (plus the same
error-handling middleware `server.js` uses) rather than requiring `server.js` itself, since
that file connects to the real `DATABASE_URL` and calls `app.listen` as a side effect of being
imported. `backend/tests/testAuthHelper.js` provides `createTestUser(role, overrides)` (a real
User document, since `requireAuth` re-queries the DB on every request) and `authHeader(user)`
(signs a token with the same payload shape as `src/utils/jwt.js`).

Run with: `npm run test:auth` (see `backend/package.json`).

| # | Test case | Steps | Expected result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Login — wrong password | POST `/api/auth/login` with a valid email, wrong password | 401; generic "Invalid email or password" |
| 2 | Login — happy path | POST `/api/auth/login` with correct credentials | 200; `data.token` present, `data.user.role` matches |
| 3 | requireAuth — no Authorization header | GET `/api/scheduling` with no header | 401 |
| 4 | requireAuth — malformed header | GET `/api/scheduling` with `Authorization: Bearer` (no token) | 401 |
| 5 | requireAuth — invalid/tampered token | GET `/api/scheduling` with a garbage token | 401 |
| 6 | Staff cannot create a schedule | POST `/api/scheduling` as Staff | 403 |
| 7 | Staff cannot delete a schedule | DELETE `/api/scheduling/:id` as Staff, even one assigned to them | 403 |
| 8 | Staff updates only `status` on their own schedule | PUT `/api/scheduling/:id` with `{status}` only, schedule assigned to that Staff user | 200; status updates, other fields (e.g. `townCouncil`) unchanged |
| 9 | Staff cannot smuggle other fields alongside `status` | PUT `/api/scheduling/:id` with `{status, townCouncil}` on their own schedule | 403; message names the rejected field |
| 10 | Staff cannot touch a schedule assigned to someone else | PUT `/api/scheduling/:id` with `{status}` on a schedule assigned to a different Staff user | 404 (not found, not "forbidden" — doesn't reveal the schedule exists) |
| 11 | Staff cannot call the endorse endpoint | PATCH `/api/rectifications/:id/endorse` as Staff on a Submitted rectification | 403 |
| 12 | Admin cannot create another Admin account | POST `/api/auth/users` as Admin with `role: "Admin"` | 403 |
| 13 | Admin can create a Staff account (positive control) | POST `/api/auth/users` as Admin with `role: "Staff"` | 201 — proves case 12's 403 is role-specific, not a blanket deny |
| 14 | Master can create an Admin account | POST `/api/auth/users` as Master with `role: "Admin"` | 201 |
| 15 | No one can create a Master account through this endpoint | POST `/api/auth/users` (as Master) with `role: "Master"` | 403 |

## Manual / exploratory checks (not automated)

| # | Test case | Expected result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 16 | Log in as each seeded role (Master/Admin/Staff) via the frontend login page | Correct tabs/actions visible per role; Accounts tab only for Master/Admin |
| 17 | Deactivate a Staff account, then use that Staff user's still-unexpired token | Next API call 401s immediately — deactivation takes effect without waiting for token expiry |
| 18 | Start the server with `JWT_SECRET` unset | Process exits immediately with a clear "FATAL: JWT_SECRET is not set" message instead of booting insecurely |

Implementation complete. Here's the full rundown:

## Backend
- **New `User` model** (`backend/src/models/users/User.js`): name/email(unique)/passwordHash/role(Master/Admin/Staff)/createdBy/isDeleted, following the app's existing soft-delete convention.
- **Auth infra**: `utils/jwt.js` (sign/verify, 8h expiry), `middleware/auth.js` (`requireAuth` re-checks the user isn't deactivated on *every* request; `requireRole(...)`), `controllers/auth/authController.js` + `routes/auth/authRoutes.js` mounted at `/api/auth` (login, me, create/list/deactivate users, with Master/Admin account-creation rules enforced server-side).
- **`server.js`** now fails fast if `JWT_SECRET` is unset (verified: exits immediately with a clear message).
- **All 5 resource routers** (lifts, defects, inspections, rectifications, scheduling) now have `requireAuth`/`requireRole` wired in per the matrix — replacing every stale TODO, including scheduling which had none at all.
- **Schedule model**: added `assignedStaffId` (real ref, indexed); `schedulingController.js` converted to the `asyncHandler`/`ApiError` pattern and now scopes `listSchedules`/`getSchedule`/`updateSchedule` to Staff ownership (confirmed additions: `getSchedule` ownership check, 404-not-403 to avoid leaking existence).
- **`inspectionController.js`**: new `assertScheduleAssignedToStaff`, applied to both `createInspection` and `updateInspection` (confirmed addition, closes the reassign-after-create loophole).
- **`backend/scripts/migrateAssignedStaff.js`**: standalone, idempotent, exact-name-match backfill (kept separate from `seed.js` deliberately, same reasoning as `cleanupOrphans()`).
- **`seed.js`**: seeds a Master, an Admin, and 4 Staff users whose names match existing `assignedInspector` strings, wiring `assignedStaffId` directly.
- **Tests**: new `tests/Auth/` suite (12 cases covering every scenario you asked for) + shared `testAuthHelper.js`; updated the 4 real existing suites (Aeric/Javier/Elijah/Ryan) to send auth headers.

## Frontend
- Real login (`AuthContext.jsx`, `LoginPage.jsx`, `AuthGate.jsx`), JWT in `localStorage`, `client.js` request/response interceptors (401 → clear token + reload, except the login call itself), logout button in the header.
- `utils/roles.js` (`ROLES`, `isAdminOrMaster`) — every "Manager" string is gone from the codebase; all 5 `canEdit` sites now express the real 3-way matrix (`canCreateOrEdit` / `canManageFull` / and Scheduling's `canManageSchedule` + `canUpdateOwnStatus` + `isOwnSchedule`).
- `EndorseButton.jsx` now Admin/Master-only.
- New Accounts screen (`AccountsPage.jsx`, `AccountFormDialog.jsx`, `authApi.js`), tab visible only to Admin/Master, with its own defense-in-depth role check.

## Verification
- Backend: **89/91 tests pass**. The 2 failures are pre-existing bugs I found but did **not** introduce or fix (confirmed via `git show HEAD`) — `nextReportNo`/`nextDefectNo` don't filter `isDeleted`, so the "reissue number after delete" tests were already broken before this change; out of scope for this RBAC pass, flagging for your awareness.
- Frontend: **73/73 tests pass**, `npm run build` succeeds cleanly.
- Confirmed the server refuses to boot without `JWT_SECRET`.

Nothing has been committed — this is all sitting in your working tree on `feature/user-management` for you to review.
